newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal parliament rejects liberalising abortion.
newsitem.headline: Portugal parliament rejects liberalising abortion.

text.p: Portugal's parliament on Thursday rejected a left-wing bid to liberalise abortion in this Roman Catholic country with a law that would have allowed pregnancies to be terminated on demand in the first 12 weeks.

After a heated six-hour debate, parliament turned down proposals by the small Communist Party and the Young Socialists, affiliated to the ruling Socialists, that would have swept away all restrictions to abortion in the first three months of pregnancy.
There was a brief moment of confusion after the vote on the Young Socialist motion which initially appeared to have ended in a tie with 111 votes in favour and 111 against.
But the final result was 112 against after one deputy, whose vote had initially been missed, was included.
"The motion has been rejected," announced parliamentary speaker Antonio Almeida Santos to cheers and jeers from rival supporters that had packed the public gallery.
A third bill extending the period in which abortions can be carried out in cases of a deformed foetus to 24 weeks from the present 16 was approved.
